sights.n: Kume Shiseibyō Confucius Temple (久米至聖廟)
sights.w: Naha's Confucian temple, a centre of Chinese learning for the Ryūkyū Kingdom since the original was built in 1671–75; its precinct holds the Meirindō, Okinawa's first public school. Rebuilt in Kume in 2013 beside Fukushū-en, on the old Chinese-émigré Kume village.
sights.k: The Ryūkyū Kingdom's Confucian temple, in old Kume village

sights.n: Naha City Museum of History (那覇市歴史博物館) — CLOSED
sights.address: Palette Kumoji 4F, 1-1-1 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Opened in 2006 to show the National Treasure 'Materials related to the Shō Family of Ryūkyū Kings' (1,166 documents and 85 art objects, including the royal crown). It closed on 31 August 2025; the treasures are due to be shown at the former Nakagusuku Udun site, opening date not yet set.
sights.k: Closed Aug 2025 — home of the Shō royal National Treasures

sights.n: Heiwa-dōri Shopping Arcade (平和通り商店街)
sights.w: Covered arcade of around 200 shops branching off Kokusai-dōri toward Makishi Public Market, nicknamed the 'labyrinth arcade'. Named 'Peace Street' by public competition in 1951 after the Heiwa-kan cinema at its mouth; a new generation of shop owners has revived it since the 2000s.

sights.n: Bin-nu-utaki / Bengadake Sacred Grove (弁之御嶽・弁ヶ嶽)
sights.w: At 165.7 m the highest point in Naha, about 1 km east of Shuri Castle. In the Ryūkyū Kingdom it was a state place of worship where the king, or his envoy, prayed for his health and the nation's peace; designated a National Historic Site as 'Bin-nu-utaki' on 15 October 2018.
sights.k: Naha's highest hill, a royal prayer site behind Shuri

sights.n: Okinawa Gokoku Shrine, Onoyama Park (沖縄県護国神社)
sights.address: Onoyama Park, Ōnoyama-chō, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: The prefecture's gokoku shrine for its war dead, set inside Onoyama Park on an islet in the Kokuba River. One of Okinawa's most-visited shrines for hatsumōde New Year prayers.
sights.k: Okinawa's shrine to the war dead, a top New Year spot

sights.w: Gusuku built by King Shō Sei in 1546 on the north mouth of Naha harbour, paired with Yarazamori Gusuku to guard the port and town. A coast-guard watchtower stands on it today, but the stone site is open to the public as a sea-view lookout.
sights.k: 1546 harbour fort, now a quiet sunset lookout

sights.n: Shuri Ryusen bingata & coral-dye studio (首里琉染)
sights.w: Bingata workshop and shop five minutes' walk from Shuri Castle Park, selling bingata and its own 'coral-dye' (sango-zome) textiles. Upstairs visitors can try coral dyeing (about 50 minutes) and watch artisans dyeing in the third-floor studio.
sights.k: Try Ryūkyū coral-dyeing beside Shuri Castle

sights.n: Yogi Park cherry blossoms (与儀公園)
sights.w: City park that is Naha's best-known cherry-blossom spot, with more than 400 Kanhizakura (Taiwan cherry) trees. They flower among Japan's earliest, and the Naha Cherry Blossom Festival is held here in early February.

sights.n: Naha Traditional Arts & Crafts Center, Tenbusu Naha (那覇市伝統工芸館)
sights.address: Tenbusu Naha 2F, 3-2-10 Makishi, Naha, Okinawa 900-0013, Japan
sights.w: City-run crafts centre on Kokusai-dōri with exhibition rooms, a shop and hands-on workshops for five Naha traditional crafts, including Ryūkyū glass, bingata, Shuri-ori weaving, lacquerware and Tsuboya pottery. Featured on the OCVB's Naha traditional-crafts walking course.
sights.k: Try five Naha crafts on Kokusai-dōri
